windows.note: No arterial/collector lane closures 7:00-9:00 a.m., 'unless otherwise approved'. Confirmed by three independent documents; identical windows to Englewood's statutory peak ban (regional convergence).

hours.override_note: 'Unless otherwise approved' — an explicit escape hatch; render as a banner, not a block (locked decision #1). The Transportation Engineering Division must approve any changes to the typical plans.

items.note: No-fee permit required — matching a city typical costs $0 and skips the review cycle (F20: the second corpus jurisdiction whose fee responds to TCP design).

CDOT Access Permit (each change in access)

fees.note: Schedule effective 2021-01-01 and prints its own staleness warning twice ('fees change periodically... call 303-987-7500 to verify') — render with that caveat. Read end to end: NO resubmittal, penalty, or expedite fee published.

applied_deltas.rule: Arrow board is required on state highways and arterial city streets (lane closure on a multi-lane street, note 7).
applied_deltas.baseline: arrow board optional per MUTCD for most single-lane closures

personnel.rule: 'Flaggers are required where poor sight distance exists (e.g., hills or curves).' A sight-distance-triggered flagger requirement — no other corpus jurisdiction triggers personnel off a geometric field condition. No TCS-preparation or certification requirement found across six documents (axis trending SILENT).

device.rule: Truck-mounted attenuator and trailer/truck flasher-or-arrow shown as (optional) on the shoulder and multi-lane typicals; END ROAD WORK sign (optional). Barricading must comply with 'City and M.U.T.C.D. Standards' (permit form standing condition — co-equal).

permit.tier_reason: tier assignment is not machine-decidable for this jurisdiction

tiers.label: Operation using typical traffic control plan
tiers.definition: Shoulder work (any street classification) or a one-lane closure on a local street, on the city's own fill-in typical — NO-FEE permit required. The typicals are optional and fee-advantaged, not mandatory ('may be useful for your submittal').

tiers.label: Operation requiring traffic control plan approval
tiers.definition: Site-specific TCP review: $26.00 and a review cycle. Ambiguity preserved (Q-LKWD-6): the no-fee list names two of the three typicals — the multi-lane-closure typical is absent, and the conservative reading is that multi-lane closures require approval regardless.

notes.rule: Entity gate: Contractor REGISTRATION (Muni Code Ch. 14.11) — registration, not a license class. Form-field verified subcontractor gate: 'List All Sub-Contractors: ___ Lakewood Lic #: ___' — every subcontractor is named on the permit with a Lakewood license number. CBC appears on the permit by name.

notes.rule: Surety: two structures — annual letter of credit / cash / guarantee letter, OR per-permit cash or LOC — with an UNPUBLISHED amount (blank field, set per permit). Render as 'surety required — amount set by the city.' An 'Investigation fee' line exists on the form with no published amount (conventionally a work-without-permit penalty; recorded, not priced).

source.doc: Lakewood Permit Application to Work in the Public Way (rev. 9/16)

notes.rule: The city's TCP form carries a named, dedicated 'Barricade Co. and Phone' field plus a 24-Hour Emergency Phone — the second Colorado jurisdiction whose official TCP artifact structurally assumes a barricade company in the loop.

Submission runs through ETRAKiT (both a public way permit AND a traffic control plan required). Adoption posture: the Engineering Standards enumerate ten CDOT M-standards and ZERO S-series — Lakewood inherits no CDOT work-zone geometry; city standard beats CDOT standard where both speak ('the City of Lakewood Design Standard shall be used').
Permit valid 180 days; eleven-month inspection; one-year warranty effective after inspection and acceptance; hot patch same day (weather permitting).

source.doc: Lakewood Permit Application to Work in the Public Way (rev. 9/16)

multi_agency.rule: The typicals distinguish state highways from city streets in two separate rules (arrow board; double posting) — state-highway work is CDOT-permit territory. A priced CDOT interface exists on the city schedule: CDOT Access Permit $75.00 each change in access.

leads.label: Inspector notice before work
leads.note: 'CALL INSPECTOR 24 HOURS IN ADVANCE OF WORK!!!' (303-987-7900) — three independent sources. This is an INSPECTION notice, not a submittal lead; conflating the two would be a material error. Plan-review turnaround is NOT PUBLISHED anywhere (five documents exhausted — genuine NL, phone-only).
